newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PICK REPORTS Q1 '97 PROFITS 40 PERCENT UP.
newsitem.headline: PICK REPORTS Q1 '97 PROFITS 40 PERCENT UP.

text.p: Hungary's leading meat processor Pick Szeged Rt group on Wednesday reported an over 40 percent rise in its pre-tax profit in the first quarter of 1997, exceeding its target.
Pick reported a consolidated pre-tax profit of 577.6 million forints for the first three months of 1997, as against 411.1 million in the same period of 1996.

"The Pick group exceeded its profit plan (of 503 million forints) by 74 million forints, while the rise was 166 million forints or 40.4 percent from the same period of last year," Pick said in its earnings report.
The group reported its sales rising to 6.68 billion forints from 5.94 billion, within which domestic sales rose 11.6 percent to 3.99 billion forints and exports by 13.9 percent to 2.69 billion.
Pick's domestic sales were marginally below its four billion forint plan, while its exports exceeded targets by 88 million.

"Our domestic sales were close to the target as we adjusted our product range to demand," Pick said, adding that better than planned prices, exchange rates and favourable product range helped its exports.

The company benefited from lower than planned purchase prices of livestock, it said. Pick planned an average price of 185 forints/kg for the first quarter of 1997 after 190 forints/kg at the end of 1996, but prices in fact were more than two forints less than planned.
